$comment: MRO schema v1 (development) — the single source of truth for every MRO collection, applied through the VALIDATED engine API by scripts/apply-mro-schema.mjs and mirrored by apps/api/test/mro-inventory.spec.ts (beforeAll). NEVER edit the live D1 with raw SQL. Development convention: the version stays at v1 until first release — keep changing THIS file (and the apply script/test mirror in the same change), never the live schema directly. What the schema currently is: (1) catalog masters mro_suppliers (vendor), mro_item_name (what the part IS — Bulb/Clutch/Tyre/Tools — and the OWNER of the stock tracking policy: tracking standard/batch/serial is declared once here and every SKU under the name inherits it; display is the bilingual pair name_en + name_mm, the retired free-text `name` column is dropped by scripts/migrate-mro-item-name-tracking.mjs); (2) mro_item_model, the SKU: the bilingual display pair name_en (indexed English, REQUIRED) + name_mm (Burmese, nullable) — migrations add them as plain ADD COLUMN and rows are backfilled (scripts/migrate-mro-model-names.mjs, which also DROPS the retired `name`/`model` columns) — plus classification via item_name (m2o to mro_item_name, REQUIRED) and expiry_alert_days — it has NO tracking column: the policy is read through item_name; (3) the multi-line document families with a draft → confirmed gate (requisitions REQ-, inbounds INB-, outbounds OUT-, transfers TRF-, adjustments AJT-) + their child line collections: a reporter (reported_by, m2o to hrm_employees) creates the doc and a SEPARATE approver (approved_by, m2o) applies signed add/remove stock changes on confirm; (4) the stock trace tables mro_stock_lots, mro_stock_serials, mro_outbound_lots/mro_outbound_serials, mro_transfer_lots/mro_transfer_serials and the mro_inventory balances. Stock is NOT managed by brand: the mro_brand master and every `brand` column (mro_item_model, mro_stock_lots, mro_stock_serials, mro_inbound_lines) are RETIRED — see removeFields + removeCollections and scripts/retire-mro-brand-remote.mjs for the remote data drop. removeCollections holds legacy leftovers dropped only when empty (the retired stocktake family mro_stocktakes/mro_stocktake_lines + the misspelled mro_requesations). The apply script is idempotent: creates missing collections, syncs newly declared fields onto existing ones (step 0c), and recreates legacy single-model movement headers only while their tables are empty.

removeFields.$comment: Fields RETIRED from a collection — dropped from the collection's field list AND from the physical table by scripts/apply-mro-schema.mjs. The MAKER (brand) is retired from the whole MRO stock domain: stock is not managed by brand, so no `brand` is captured on a receipt, stamped on a lot/serial or classified on a SKU.

baseCollections.name: MRO Item Categories
baseCollections.description: Catalog top-level grouping: what broad category a part family belongs to — Engine & Gear Box, Body & Lighting, Grease & Fluids, ... Each mro_item_name (part group) points at ONE category via its category m2o; the stock/filter UI buckets items as model -> item_name -> category. Reference by mro_item_name.category. `issues_type` is the ROLE flag: true marks a category that also applies to maintenance issue types (veh_issue_types.category), so the Maintenance hub's Issues strip / job picker offer it; false (the default) is a catalog-only category, excluded there.

fields.name: issues_type
fields.label: Issues Type
fields.description: Whether this category applies to maintenance ISSUE TYPES (job families). true ⇒ the Maintenance hub's Issues strip and the log form's job picker may use it; false (the default) is a catalog-only category — a part family bucket that never appears as a job category.

baseCollections.name: MRO Suppliers
baseCollections.description: Vendor master — referenced by mro_inbounds.supplier. Inbound documents record where stock came from.

baseCollections.name: MRO Item Name
baseCollections.description: Catalog master: what the part IS - Bulb, Clutch, Chamber, Tyre, Tools, ... AND the owner of the stock TRACKING POLICY: `tracking` (standard/batch/serial) is declared ONCE here and every SKU under the name INHERITS it - mro_item_model has no tracking column, the confirm engine + the SKU pickers read it through mro_item_model.item_name. So a name defined as serial can never have a standard SKU. Display: the bilingual pair name_en (indexed English, the name every picker shows) + name_mm (Burmese); the retired free-text `name` column is dropped by scripts/migrate-mro-item-name-tracking.mjs, which also backfills name_en from it. name_en is REQUIRED (indexed, the name every picker shows) — it is the master's identity and BOTH writers (the masters-hub form and the SKU picker's quick-add) always set it; name_mm (the Burmese label) stays optional. `tracking` is ALSO REQUIRED, with default `standard` — the policy is never absent: a client that omits it gets standard from the column DEFAULT, so it stays optional ON THE WIRE while the column is NOT NULL. (Making an existing nullable column NOT NULL needs a one-off, because the apply script's field sync only ADDs: scripts/migrate-mro-item-name-required.mjs for name_en and scripts/migrate-mro-item-name-tracking-required.mjs for tracking.) Each name belongs to a top-level mro_item_categories group via its category m2o. Referenced by mro_item_model.item_name.

fields.name: tracking
fields.label: Tracking Policy
fields.description: The stock policy EVERY SKU under this name inherits — standard (plain balance), batch (lot + expiry), serial (one row per unit). Set once here; the SKU form never asks. REQUIRED with default standard: a name can never exist in a "no policy" state — new rows backfill standard from the DEFAULT, so a name with no models is plainly stocked until someone deliberately reclassifies it.

fields.name: assets
fields.label: Tracked as Asset
fields.description: Declared ONCE per item name: true ⇒ this item is a CUSTODY-BEARING asset — every unit is a real, individually-tracked physical thing (a tyre, a jack, a toolbox) that can be held by a truck, a wheel position or an employee, and carries a condition. Mirrors `tracking`: the policy lives here and every SKU under the name inherits it. RULE: assets = true REQUIRES tracking = serial (an asset is one row per unit by definition); the SKU/name forms enforce + lock it. The asset register (`GET /api/mro/assets/holder`) filters on this flag, so standard/batch consumables (Engine Oil, Bolt) never appear on a truck's or person's asset list.

baseCollections.name: MRO Item Model
baseCollections.description: The MRO stock-keeping unit (SKU): one model per tracked part. The stock TRACKING POLICY is NOT declared here — it lives on the item name (`mro_item_name.tracking`) and every SKU under that name inherits it, so a Tyre SKU is serial forever and nobody re-picks a policy per model; the confirm engine + pickers resolve it through the item_name relation. expiry_alert_days is the per-model alert window read by /api/mro/stock/expiring. Classification: item_name (m2o to mro_item_name, REQUIRED — a SKU with no item name would have no tracking policy). Display: a bilingual pair — name_en (the indexed English name document lines show) + name_mm (Burmese); the retired free-text `name`/`model` columns are dropped by scripts/migrate-mro-model-names.mjs.

fields.name: item_name
fields.label: Item Name
fields.description: The item-name master this SKU hangs under — ALSO the source of its stock tracking policy (mro_item_name.tracking). Required: a SKU with no item name has no policy.

fields.name: reference_tread_mm
fields.label: New-tread depth (mm)
fields.description: A serial-tracked tyre's depth when new — the baseline the fitment board uses to derive a unit's remaining-tread %. Only filled for serial (tyre) SKUs; standard/batch models leave it null.

baseCollections.name: MRO Inventory
baseCollections.description: Aggregate on-hand balance per (item_model, location) plus the reorder_level policy. Balance rows are created/maintained by the confirm services; reorder_level is operator-set and read by /api/mro/stock/onhand (below_reorder).

baseCollections.name: MRO Stock Lots
baseCollections.description: Lot-level stock trace for batch-tracked models: one row per (batch_no, location) with the remaining qty, expiry date and provenance (source inbound + line, unit cost). Confirm services are the sole writers.

baseCollections.name: MRO Stock Serials
baseCollections.description: Unit-level stock trace for serial-tracked models: one globally-unique row per unit with its location, status and provenance. Confirm services are the sole writers.

fields.name: employee
fields.label: Held By Employee
fields.description: Person custody — the employee who currently HOLDS this asset (a tyre or any `assets` item issued out to a person, not fitted to a truck). INVARIANT: a unit is held by EITHER a vehicle (+slot) OR an employee, never both; the writers enforce it. The holder is DERIVED on read (employee ? person : vehicle ? truck+slot : store location) — never stored, so it can never drift.

fields.name: tread_mm
fields.label: Tread depth (mm)
fields.description: Latest measured tread depth on this serial tyre (a `checked` inspection snapshot). Null until the first inspection; never estimated.

fields.name: psi
fields.label: Pressure (psi)
fields.description: Latest measured inflation pressure on this serial tyre (`checked` snapshot).

fields.name: condition
fields.label: Condition
fields.description: Latest measured wear/condition of this asset unit (`checked` snapshot) — the equipment counterpart of a tyre's tread_mm/psi. Kept for EVERY asset (tyres included) so a jack/toolbox has a condition even though it has no tread. Null until the first inspection; never estimated.

baseCollections.name: MRO Outbound Lots
baseCollections.description: Outbound lot trace — which active lot satisfied each outbound line and how much it gave. Written by the confirm service.

baseCollections.name: MRO Outbound Serials
baseCollections.description: Outbound serial trace — which in-stock unit left per outbound line. Written by the confirm service.

recreateCollections.name: MRO Inbounds
recreateCollections.description: Stock-in document header (draft → confirmed → cancelled). Lines live in mro_inbound_lines; inventory is touched ONLY by /api/mro/inbounds/:id/confirm. The engine's core doc_status rules already guarantee generic writes can never reach "confirmed" (only draft → cancelled); the confirm service is the sole writer of "confirmed".

fields.name: supplier
fields.label: Supplier
fields.description: The VENDOR this receipt was bought from. Only a `purchase` has one: the engine's `required_if` rule below makes a purchase without a supplier a 400, while a `legacy` (opening balance) or `return` doc leaves it empty and records `handed_by` instead — there is no vendor on goods coming back from a person.

fields.name: handed_by
fields.label: Handed by
fields.description: The EMPLOYEE on a receipt that has no vendor. `return` = the goods came back FROM this person (they handed them back); `legacy` (opening balance) = this person hands over the existing stock being booked in. The two `required_if` rules below make it mandatory for those kinds and irrelevant for a `purchase` — the counterparty of an inbound is ALWAYS a supplier or an employee, never both, never neither. Distinct from `received_by`, which the confirm route stamps from the session (the store side who booked it in).

fields.name: paid_at_receipt
fields.label: Paid at Receipt
fields.description: The money came WITH the goods: the CONFIRM files ONE payment (mro_inbound_payments) equal to the line total, dated the receipt date, so the receipt arrives settled — nothing left to pay and no second step at the counter. Meaningful for a purchase only (a return / opening balance owes nobody) and only with a positive total; a confirmed receipt is frozen (`writes.freeze_when`), so this is a DRAFT-only decision, never a later switch.

fields.name: paid_amount
fields.label: Paid Amount
fields.description: ENGINE-MAINTAINED (never a client field): the sum of this receipt's live `mro_inbound_payments.amount`. Recomputed by the compiled denorm hook on every payment write, so the card's Paid figure can never drift from the ledger.

fields.name: payment_status
fields.label: Payment Status
fields.description: ENGINE-MAINTAINED: `unpaid` (nothing paid yet, or no total to compare against), `partial` (0 < paid < total) or `paid` (paid ≥ total). Derived by the payment denorm hook from the ledger + `total_amount`.

fields.name: fully_paid_on
fields.label: Fully Paid On
fields.description: ENGINE-MAINTAINED: the DAY the receipt became fully paid — the latest ledger entry's `paid_on` at the moment the running total reached `total_amount` (which is why a settled older invoice keeps the day it was actually cleared). Cleared again if a payment is removed and the receipt is no longer settled.

fields.name: received_by
fields.label: Received By
fields.description: Session-stamped on confirm (the /inbounds/:id/confirm route passes actorOf) — a receipt records WHO booked the stock in, mirroring mro_outbounds.issued_by.

fields.name: cancelled_at
fields.label: Cancelled At
fields.description: Service-written on /api/mro/inbounds/:id/cancel — the moment the receipt ended. For a CONFIRMED receipt this is also the moment its stock effect was undone (the reversal), so the stamp and the reversal are one atomic fact, never two.

fields.name: cancelled_by
fields.label: Cancelled By
fields.description: Session-stamped on cancel — cancelling a POSTED receipt moves stock back, so who did it is as material as who confirmed it (received_by). Never sent by a client.

recreateCollections.name: MRO Outbounds
recreateCollections.description: Stock-out document header (draft → confirmed → cancelled). Lines live in mro_outbound_lines; stock is deducted ONLY by /api/mro/outbounds/:id/confirm. The engine's core doc_status rules already guarantee generic writes can never reach "confirmed" (only draft → cancelled); the confirm service is the sole writer of "confirmed".

fields.name: cancelled_at
fields.label: Cancelled At
fields.description: Service-written on /api/mro/outbounds/:id/cancel — the moment the issue ended. For a CONFIRMED issue this is also the moment its stock effect was undone (every allocated lot returned, every issued unit back in stock), so the stamp and the reversal are one atomic fact.

fields.name: cancelled_by
fields.label: Cancelled By
fields.description: Session-stamped on cancel — cancelling a POSTED issue puts stock back, so who did it is as material as who confirmed it (issued_by). Never sent by a client.

newCollections.name: MRO Inbound Lines
newCollections.description: Inbound document line — one row per received item on the draft. Engine child of mro_inbounds (parent_id). Stock effects apply at confirm.

newCollections.name: MRO Outbound Lines
newCollections.description: Outbound document line — one row per item to issue/write off on the draft. Engine child of mro_outbounds (parent_id). Stock is deducted at confirm.

moreCollections.name: MRO Transfers
moreCollections.description: Location-to-location stock transfer document header (draft → confirmed → cancelled). Lines live in mro_transfer_lines; stock moves ONLY at /api/mro/transfers/:id/confirm — the source store deducts, the destination store receives, and lot/serial identity survives the move. A CONFIRMED move is undone by POST /api/mro/transfers/:id/cancel, which reverses it from its own lot/serial trace in the same atomic batch that flips it to cancelled.

fields.name: cancelled_at
fields.label: Cancelled At
fields.description: Service-written on /api/mro/transfers/:id/cancel — the moment the move ended. For a CONFIRMED transfer this is also the moment its stock effect was undone (source lots back, destination lots down, units back to the source store), so the stamp and the reversal are one atomic fact, never two.

fields.name: cancelled_by
fields.label: Cancelled By
fields.description: Session-stamped on cancel — cancelling a POSTED move puts stock back, so who did it is as material as who confirmed it (approved_by). Never sent by a client.

moreCollections.name: MRO Transfer Lines
moreCollections.description: Transfer document line — one row per moved item on the draft. Engine child of mro_transfers (parent_id). For batch models an optional batch_no restricts the move to that batch; serial models list the exact serials.

moreCollections.name: MRO Transfer Lots
moreCollections.description: Lot-level transfer trace — which source lot fed the move and which destination lot (created or merged into) received it, per transfer line.

moreCollections.name: MRO Transfer Serials
moreCollections.description: Serial-level transfer trace — every moved unit and its transfer line.

moreCollections.name: MRO Adjustments
moreCollections.description: Stock adjustment document header (draft → confirmed → cancelled), the lean replacement for the retired physical-count stocktake. An operator reports the correction (reported_by/description); a SEPARATE user must approve it (approved_by). Confirming applies the signed per-line changes to the header location in ONE atomic batch — add raises the balance (creating a lot for batch models), remove lowers it (batch lots written off FEFO, serial units set un-in-stock) — and each line stores the expected_qty/diff_qty it reconciled.

fields.name: cancelled_at
fields.label: Cancelled At
fields.description: Service-written on /api/mro/adjustments/:id/cancel — the moment the correction ended. For an APPROVED adjustment this is also the moment its ± stock effect was undone (added lots removed, removed lots restored, un-stocked units back in stock), so the stamp and the reversal are one atomic fact.

fields.name: cancelled_by
fields.label: Cancelled By
fields.description: Session-stamped on cancel — cancelling an APPROVED adjustment moves stock back, so who did it is as material as who approved it (approved_by). Never sent by a client.

moreCollections.name: MRO Adjustment Lines
moreCollections.description: Adjustment document line — one signed change (direction add/remove + positive qty) to one item model at the header store. Engine child of mro_adjustments (parent_id). Batch models need a batch identity on add; serial models list the exact serials to remove. expected_qty/diff_qty are written by the confirm service so the confirmed document records what it applied.

moreCollections.name: MRO Adjustment Lots
moreCollections.description: Adjustment lot trace — which active lot each adjustment line moved and how much: an `add` line's newly created lot, or one FEFO take of a `remove` line. Written by the confirm service and the ONLY thing a reversal reads to put stock back, so an approved adjustment is undone exactly (never re-derived from a FEFO guess that would hit different lots).

moreCollections.name: MRO Adjustment Serials
moreCollections.description: Adjustment serial trace — which in-stock unit each adjustment line removed. Written by the confirm service; the reversal reads it (plus the unit's own state guard) to restore exactly those units.

moreCollections.name: MRO Requisitions
moreCollections.description: Stock request document header (draft → confirmed = approved → cancelled). Lines live in mro_requisition_lines; confirming (approving) NEVER touches stock — it validates the lines, records the approver and writes the totals + flips doc_status, so an approved requisition is the authority a later goods-issue outbound fulfils. The engine's core doc_status rules keep 'confirmed' service-only; requisition_status (requested → approved → partially_issued/fulfilled) is the user-facing lifecycle driven by the service on approve and on goods-issue confirm.

moreCollections.name: MRO Requisition Lines
moreCollections.description: Requisition document line — one row per requested item on the draft. Engine child of mro_requisitions (parent_id). Stock is never reserved at confirm; qty is the requested quantity.

moreCollections.name: MRO Asset Requests
moreCollections.description: Asset custody REQUEST — the approval gate a governed asset change must pass before it happens. ONE table serves all THREE governed shapes, and the request's KIND is DERIVED from its destination: `write_off` ⇒ a WRITE-OFF (the unit is scrapped where it sits, no destination named); `to_location` ⇒ a RETURN (holder → store); `to_vehicle`/`to_employee` ⇒ a TRANSFER (truck→truck, person→person, truck→person or person→truck are NOT offered). Filed through the generic entity API: `requested_by` is stamped from the session and `status`/`approved_by`/`approved_at`/`rejected_reason`/`executed_at` are FROZEN against generic writes (only this service sets them). A recorded superior of the requester decides it via POST /api/mro/asset-requests/:id/approve|reject (an admin may decide any), then POST /api/mro/asset-requests/:id/execute performs the move, the return or the write-off in ONE atomic batch pinned to the recorded source (`from_*`) and appends the serial's lifecycle event tagged ref_kind='ATR' + this request's display_number.

fields.name: from_vehicle
fields.label: From Vehicle
fields.description: The source the request was filed against — the move is pinned to it at execute, so a unit that moved elsewhere in the meantime is NEVER silently relocated from the new place.

fields.name: to_location
fields.label: Return To Store
fields.description: The STORE this unit is being RETURNED to — set instead of `to_vehicle`/`to_employee`, and the field that makes this request a RETURN rather than a transfer. The requester names WHERE; the execute honours exactly it.

fields.name: write_off
fields.label: Write Off
fields.description: Set ⇒ this request is a WRITE-OFF (scrap), not a move: the unit ends its life where it sits, so every destination column (`to_vehicle`/`to_slot`/`to_employee`/`to_location`) stays NULL (a compiled guard refuses the contradiction in BOTH directions). Filing changes nothing; the superior's approve is the sign-off and the execute performs `issued → scrapped`, clears the seat + holder, and appends ONE `written_off` event tagged ref_kind='ATR' + this request's display_number.

fields.name: requested_by
fields.label: Requested By
fields.description: Session-stamped (policies.actor_fields) — a requester can never file a request as someone else, which is what makes the superior check meaningful.

moreCollections.name: MRO Inbound Payments
moreCollections.description: PAYMENT LEDGER of a purchase receipt — one row per payment made against `mro_inbounds.total_amount`: WHEN it was paid (`paid_on`), HOW MUCH (`amount`), how (`method`, `reference`) and WHO recorded it (`recorded_by`, session-stamped). Filed through the generic entity API and IMMUTABLE once filed — the compiled `before_update` guard in `inbound-payments.ts` refuses any change to the defining columns, so a wrong entry is soft-deleted (it leaves the live set) and re-filed rather than rewritten; `reference` / `note` stay correctable. The same module's denorm hooks then re-derive the header's `paid_amount` / `payment_status` / `fully_paid_on` from the LIVE ledger, which is what the receipt card's progress bar and Total/Paid/Left breakdown read. Only a purchase has one (a return / opening balance owes nobody).

fields.name: parent_id
fields.label: Receipt
fields.description: The purchase receipt this payment belongs to — `cascade_delete` so deleting a receipt can never orphan its ledger.

fields.name: reference
fields.label: Reference
fields.description: Cheque no / bank transfer ref — free text, optional.

fields.name: recorded_by
fields.label: Recorded By
fields.description: Session-stamped (policies.actor_fields) — who booked this payment in, un-forgeable.

moreCollections.name: VEH Accidents & Incidents
moreCollections.description: Real accident/incident record bound to the veh_fleets plate directory (the legacy phantom vehicle_incidents was removed). One row covers both kinds via the kind select (accident | incident); a reporter (hrm_employees) files it, the personnel m2m (hrm_employees) carries the crew involved, severity/location/est_cost describe it, incident_date anchors the timeline. Read-only list screen: /app/incidents.

moreCollections.name: VEH Permits (Licenses)
moreCollections.description: Real vehicle license/permit record bound to the veh_fleets plate directory (the legacy phantom vehicle_permits was removed). One row is one license document on a vehicle: a permit_no, where it was issued (place), and the issue/expiry dates anchor the renewal countdown. Read-only list screen: /app/licenses.

moreCollections.name: VEH Insurances
moreCollections.description: Real vehicle insurance policy record bound to the veh_fleets plate directory (the legacy phantom vehicle_insurances was removed). One row is one policy on a vehicle: provider + policy_no identity and an expiry_date that drives the renewal countdown. Read-only list screen: /app/insurances.

moreCollections.name: VEH Odo Months
moreCollections.description: Daily odometer readings per veh_fleets vehicle, bucketed ONE row per (vehicle, Gregorian month) — the row's `readings` JSON array holds that month's daily readings [{date, odo, note?, at?}]. A vehicle's current odo = the newest-date entry across its month rows, the read-side floor every km service interval counts from (replaces the old row-per-reading veh_odo_logs model).

moreCollections.name: VEH Fluid Fills
moreCollections.description: Engine-oil / gear-oil fill history per veh_fleets vehicle (the Fleet Care Fluid app writes them) — one row per fill with the odometer at which the service happened (odo_at_fill) and the odometer at which the NEXT service of that kind is due (next_due_odo, chosen per fill — no fixed per-vehicle interval). km-left is derived read-side from that newest fill's next_due_odo.

fields.name: date
fields.label: Effective Date
fields.description: The day the service was performed (YYYY-MM-DD). Older rows without it fall back to created_at for their history date.

fields.name: next_due_odo
fields.label: Next Due Odo (km)
fields.description: The odometer at which the NEXT service of this kind is due — set per fill.

moreCollections.name: MRO Serial Events
moreCollections.description: Immutable per-serial lifecycle history feed (the single source of truth for 'where each unit has been and what happened to it'). The mro_stock_serials row always holds the live snapshot; every MRO service confirm that changes a serial's state appends ONE event row here in the same atomic D1 batch (and reversible on guard failure). Events: purchased, returned, fitted, store_transferred, rotated, refitted, written_off, adjusted.

fields.name: tread_mm
fields.label: Tread depth (mm)
fields.description: Measured tread depth at this `checked` inspection (a measurement field on the event row).

fields.name: condition
fields.label: Condition
fields.description: The asset's condition reading AT THIS event (a `checked` inspection) — the equipment counterpart of tread_mm/psi, kept on the immutable history row so the timeline reports what was seen then.

fields.name: from_employee
fields.label: From Employee
fields.description: The employee who HELD this asset before the event (custody lineage) — the person counterpart of from_vehicle.

fields.name: to_employee
fields.label: To Employee
fields.description: The employee who RECEIVED this asset at the event (custody lineage) — the person counterpart of to_vehicle.

fields.name: event_date
fields.label: Event Date
fields.description: The day the movement physically happened (YYYY-MM-DD) when the operator back-dates a fit/un-seat; every other event leaves it empty and the history falls back to created_at.

moreCollections.name: VEH Issue Types
moreCollections.description: Maintenance issue-type master (the job catalog): each row is one standard maintenance job a truck log can cite — a required job_code (the operator's short code), a bilingual display pair (name_en + name_mm), a category (m2o to mro_item_categories, restricted in the UI to categories flagged issues_type) and free keywords for lookup. veh_maintenance_logs.issues_type points here. Read by the ပြင်ဆင် app's log-form picker; seeded with the three baseline jobs.

moreCollections.name: VEH Maintenance Logs
moreCollections.description: Vehicle maintenance log — ONE repair/service job performed on a veh_fleets truck. started_at/end_at anchor the downtime window, odo records the odometer at the job, issues_type (m2o veh_issue_types) names the standard job, driver records who drove the truck in, technician + vendor_type say who did the work, parts_cost + labor_cost are the operator's inputs and total_cost is a STORED formula (parts_cost + labor_cost — engine-recomputed on every write, never client-written). approved_by / recommended_by are the hrm_employees sign-off pair. Read + written by the ပြင်ဆင် app (/app/maintenances); a row stays editable while `doc_status` is `draft`, then is CONFIRMED (draft → confirmed) and frozen by the `writes.freeze_when` policy below — a posted job is never rewritten, it is corrected out of band.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.label: Total Cost
fields.description: Engine-owned stored formula: parts_cost + labor_cost, recomputed on every create/update. Never client-written.
